articles.summary: International Sports News: Alex Apodaca just pulled off the kind of result that completely flips a fight card on its head. At DWCS Season 10, Week 3, Apodaca walked into the Met.
articles.body: Alex Apodaca just pulled off the kind of result that completely flips a fight card on its head. At DWCS Season 10, Week 3, Apodaca walked into the Meta APEX as the massive underdog against Bella Mir. UFC's official results had Mir listed as a -6000 favorite, so the expectation was pretty clear before the cage door closed. Three rounds later, Apodaca had all three judges on her side. She won 29-28 across the board and left with something even bigger than the win: a UFC contract.How Alex Apodaca broke down Bella Mir over three roundsThe fight did not turn into an easy night for Apodaca. Mir still managed to land some heavy shots, but Apodaca found ways to make the matchup difficult for her.According to the UFC's official recap, Apodaca kept switching stances and mixed up her striking rather than giving Mir the same look over and over. Her takedown defense was also a major part of the performance. That kept Mir from relying too heavily on her grappling and allowed Apodaca to keep the fight in areas where she was more effective.Nothing was left to a single dramatic moment. The bout went the entire three rounds, with the judges all reaching the same 29-28 score for Apodaca. That consistency made the result even more striking considering the enormous betting gap coming into the contest.Bella Mir leaves with first professional MMA defeatFor Mir, the loss changes an unbeaten record she had carried into the fight. She entered DWCS with a 3-0 professional MMA mark and also had an established name in the sport through her father, former UFC heavyweight champion Frank Mir.After the decision, Mir dropped to 3-1. Apodaca, meanwhile, moved to 8-1 and turned the biggest opportunity of her young career into a place on the UFC roster.Dana White later confirmed contracts for Apodaca along with Nick Galanti, Ronald Humphrey, Sean Clancy Jr., and Guilherme Uriel.Galanti needed only 35 seconds to earn his contract with a knockout. Clancy Jr. finished Gary Balletto in Round 2, while Uriel submitted Mario Piazzon with a standing guillotine.That leaves Apodaca with a very different kind of result. She did not need a finish. She survived three rounds against a heavily favored opponent, got every judge's score, and secured her UFC spot in the process.For now, the biggest number beside her name is simple: 8-1. articles.body:
Bella Mir has missed out on a UFC contract after suffering one of the biggest shocks in MMA history by losing to Alex Apodaca.

Highly-rated prospect Mir, who is the daughter of former UFC heavyweight champion Frank, went into the contest as an overwhelming favourite but was on the losing end of a unanimous decision.

All three judges on Dana White's Contender Series - a show where winners of fights are often rewarded with UFC contracts - scored the contest 29-28 in American Apodaca's favour.

Mir, 23, has said she wants to win a UFC championship, a Brazilian jiu-jitsu title, a Zuffa Boxing belt and an Olympic wrestling gold medal, but the loss puts a dent in the American's ambitions.

After the fight, UFC president Dana White said the pre-fight betting odds, which had Mir as a massive favourite to win, were misplaced.

"You can't have those kind of underdogs on this show. Anything is possible, and if the Bella Mir fight didn't just prove it - the odds were way out of whack," said White.

"This sport's too crazy to be that big of an underdog."

Apodaca, 32, was rewarded with a UFC contract following victory, while Mir suffered the first defeat of her five-fight professional MMA career.

Elsewhere, Scotland's Sean Clancy Jr won a UFC contract after he stopped American Gary Balletto in the second round following a number of unanswered ground strikes.

The 23-year-old, who is the welterweight champion in UK-based promotion Cage Warriors, extended the unbeaten start to his career to nine.
